claims.text: The target material is a multicomponent high-entropy material initially in a solid state.
Machine-learning algorithms would be applied to predict thermodynamic properties.
Machine-learning algorithms can learn patterns in thermodynamic data.
Learned thermodynamic patterns enable predictions for multicomponent high-entropy materials.
The machine-learning predictions would be derived from materials-science principles.
Machine learning would improve determination of transition temperature relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Machine learning would improve determination of fusion enthalpy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Machine learning would improve determination of fusion entropy relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Machine learning would improve determination of volume change at the transition relative to current experimental and computational methods.
Machine learning would improve determination of dense-fluid heat capacity relative to current experimental and computational methods.
The proposed approach is scoped to high temperatures and multicomponent systems.
Training data for the proposed machine-learning approach may be limited.
The complexity of high-entropy materials may cause prediction errors.
Comparing machine-learning predictions with experimental measurements for a specific multicomponent high-entropy material would test the hypothesis.
A significant deviation between machine-learning predictions and experimental measurements would falsify the hypothesis.
